runsheet.short_description: Disconnect webinar audio+video from the room. (Display the holding slide.)
Meet to know one another. [[Tutorial Moderator]] confirm where [[Zoom Master]] will sit.
In the Zoom webinar, promote the tutorial presenters and [[Tutorial Moderator]] to panelist. Disable Zoom Chat and raised hand (for attendees).
runsheet.more_info:
Chat > menu > attendees can chat with: nobody. Host Tools > attendees > raise hand: off.
Use use [#panelist-names](https://ismir2026.slack.com/archives/C0CER5XPX19)

runsheet.short_description: Greet the presenters (on-site and online). For online presenters: test audio+video input+output and screenshare (and sound share if they play audio). For on-site presenters: test the room laptop/HDMI and slides.
runsheet.more_info: Online presenters are asked to join the webinar 10 minutes in advance and wait for promotion. Ask presenters about their planned breaks and Q&A points, and note them.

runsheet.short_description: Grab a mic and keep it for the whole session. Join Zoom on the provided laptop and disconnect audio+video (see screenshots). Keep the Q&A panel (screenshot) open at all times.
runsheet.more_info: ![Click the arrow next to Audio](images/audio_menu.png) ![Choose "Leave computer audio"](images/leave_computer_audio.png) ![The Q&A button in Zoom](images/q&a_button.png)

runsheet.short_description: Connect webinar audio+video to the room.
Announce the tutorial starts. Introduce yourself as the volunteer who moderates the tutorial. Introduce the presenters and let them take over.

Act as the on-site proxy for online presenters: relay what happens in the room (e.g. audio/slide issues, audience reactions) and speak up when the presenter cannot be heard or seen. If a panelist account is making noises, mute it.
Sit in the corner of the audience. Watch the webinar and the room screen; fix mismatches immediately.
Take on-site questions first, then online questions from the Zoom Q&A panel. No need to switch back and forth. Give your mic to on-site askers; read online questions aloud.
Announce when the tutorial resumes. Display the holding slide during the break.
